        "contents": "\n\n/**\n * Use FireCrawl's native deep research feature\n * This is a simplified wrapper around FireCrawl's deep research API\n */\nexport const advancedDeepResearch = async (\n\tquery: string,\n\toptions: {\n\t\tmaxDepth?: number;\n\t\tmaxUrls?: number;\n\t\ttimeLimit?: number;\n\t},\n) =\u003e {\n\tconst deepResearchOptions: FireDeepResearchOptions = {\n\t\tquery,\n\t\tmaxDepth: options.maxDepth || 5,\n\t\tmaxUrls: options.maxUrls || 15,\n\t\ttimeLimit: options.timeLimit || 180,\n\t};\n\t// Define a callback for activity updates\n\tconst onActivity = (activity: unknown) =\u003e {\n\t\tif (\n\t\t\ttypeof activity === \"object\" \u0026\u0026\n\t\t\tactivity !== null \u0026\u0026\n\t\t\t\"type\" in activity \u0026\u0026\n\t\t\t\"message\" in activity\n\t\t) {\n\t\t\t// @ts-expect-error: dynamic shape\n\t\t\tconsole.log(&#96;[${activity.type}] ${activity.message}&#96;);\n\t\t}\n\t};\n\treturn await fireDeepResearch(query, deepResearchOptions, onActivity);\n};",

      "codeBlock": {
        "contents": "    echo \"$processed_urls\" | while read -r media_url; do\n        # Skip empty lines\n        [[ -z \"$media_url\" ]] \u0026\u0026 continue\n        \n        # Extract filename from URL\n        local filename=$(basename \"$media_url\" | sed 's/\\?.*//')\n        \n        echo -e \"${YELLOW}[$count/$url_count] Downloading:${NC} $filename\"\n        \n        # Download with curl, showing progress bar\n        curl -L --progress-bar \"$media_url\" -o \"$media_dir/$filename\"\n        \n        # Check if download was successful\n        if [[ $? -eq 0 ]]; then\n            echo -e \"${GREEN}Successfully downloaded:${NC} $filename\"\n        else\n            echo -e \"${RED}Failed to download:${NC} $filename\"\n        fi\n        \n        count=$((count+1))\n    done\n}\n\n# Function to use Firecrawl Extract API\nuse_firecrawl_extract() {\n    local url=\"$1\"\n    local domain=$(sanitize_domain_name \"$url\")\n    \n    echo -e \"${YELLOW}Using Firecrawl Extract API for $url...${NC}\"\n    \n    # Create domain-specific directory for multiple URLs\n    if [[ ${#URLS[@]} -gt 1 ]]; then\n        mkdir -p \"$DOWNLOAD_DIR/extracted/$domain\"\n        local extract_dir=\"$DOWNLOAD_DIR/extracted/$domain\"\n    else\n        local extract_dir=\"$DOWNLOAD_DIR/extracted\"\n    fi\n    \n    # Prepare the request to Firecrawl Extract API\n    local response=$(curl -s -X POST https://api.firecrawl.dev/v1/extract \\\n        -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n        -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" \\\n        -d \"{\\\"urls\\\": [\\\"$url\\\"], \\\"formats\\\": [\\\"all\\\"]}\")\n    \n    # Check if the API call was successful\n    if [[ $response == *\"error\"* ]]; then\n        echo -e \"${RED}Error from Firecrawl API:${NC} $response\"\n        return\n    fi\n    \n    # Create a sanitized filename based on the URL\n    local sanitized_filename=$(echo \"$url\" | sed 's/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/_/g')\n    \n    # Save the full API response as JSON\n    echo \"$response\" \u003e \"$extract_dir/${sanitized_filename}_full_response.json\"\n    \n    # Extract text content from the API response\n    local text_content=$(echo \"$response\" | grep -o '\"text\":\"[^\"]*\"' | sed 's/\"text\":\"//;s/\"$//' | sed 's/\\\\n/\\n/g')\n    \n    # Save the text content\n    echo \"$text_content\" \u003e \"$extract_dir/${sanitized_filename}_content.txt\"\n    \n    # Extract title from the API response\n    local title=$(echo \"$response\" | grep -o '\"title\":\"[^\"]*\"' | sed 's/\"title\":\"//;s/\"$//')\n    \n    # Save page metadata\n    echo \"URL: $url\" \u003e \"$extract_dir/${sanitized_filename}_metadata.txt\"\n    echo \"Title: $title\" \u003e\u003e \"$extract_dir/${sanitized_filename}_metadata.txt\"\n    echo \"Extraction Date: $(date)\" \u003e\u003e \"$extract_dir/${sanitized_filename}_metadata.txt\"\n    \n    echo -e \"${GREEN}Successfully extracted content from $url${NC}\"\n    echo -e \"${GREEN}Saved to:${NC} $extract_dir/${sanitized_filename}_content.txt\"\n}\n\n# Process each URL\n",

            "text": "# Process each URL"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 365
          }
        ],
        "originalContents": "    echo \"$processed_urls\" | while read -r media_url; do\n        # Skip empty lines\n        [[ -z \"$media_url\" ]] \u0026\u0026 continue\n        \n        # Extract filename from URL\n        local filename=$(basename \"$media_url\" | sed 's/\\?.*//')\n        \n        echo -e \"${YELLOW}[$count/$url_count] Downloading:${NC} $filename\"\n        \n        # Download with curl, showing progress bar\n        curl -L --progress-bar \"$media_url\" -o \"$media_dir/$filename\"\n        \n        # Check if download was successful\n        if [[ $? -eq 0 ]]; then\n            echo -e \"${GREEN}Successfully downloaded:${NC} $filename\"\n        else\n            echo -e \"${RED}Failed to download:${NC} $filename\"\n        fi\n        \n        count=$((count+1))\n    done\n}\n\n# Function to use Firecrawl Extract API\nuse_firecrawl_extract() {\n    local url=\"$1\"\n    local domain=$(sanitize_domain_name \"$url\")\n    \n    echo -e \"${YELLOW}Using Firecrawl Extract API for $url...${NC}\"\n    \n    # Create domain-specific directory for multiple URLs\n    if [[ ${#URLS[@]} -gt 1 ]]; then\n        mkdir -p \"$DOWNLOAD_DIR/extracted/$domain\"\n        local extract_dir=\"$DOWNLOAD_DIR/extracted/$domain\"\n    else\n        local extract_dir=\"$DOWNLOAD_DIR/extracted\"\n    fi\n    \n    # Prepare the request to Firecrawl Extract API\n    local response=$(curl -s -X POST https://api.firecrawl.dev/v1/extract \\\n        -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n        -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" \\\n        -d \"{\\\"urls\\\": [\\\"$url\\\"], \\\"formats\\\": [\\\"all\\\"]}\")\n    \n    # Check if the API call was successful\n    if [[ $response == *\"error\"* ]]; then\n        echo -e \"${RED}Error from Firecrawl API:${NC} $response\"\n        return\n    fi\n    \n    # Create a sanitized filename based on the URL\n    local sanitized_filename=$(echo \"$url\" | sed 's/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/_/g')\n    \n    # Save the full API response as JSON\n    echo \"$response\" \u003e \"$extract_dir/${sanitized_filename}_full_response.json\"\n    \n    # Extract text content from the API response\n    local text_content=$(echo \"$response\" | grep -o '\"text\":\"[^\"]*\"' | sed 's/\"text\":\"//;s/\"$//' | sed 's/\\\\n/\\n/g')\n    \n    # Save the text content\n    echo \"$text_content\" \u003e \"$extract_dir/${sanitized_filename}_content.txt\"\n    \n    # Extract title from the API response\n    local title=$(echo \"$response\" | grep -o '\"title\":\"[^\"]*\"' | sed 's/\"title\":\"//;s/\"$//')\n    \n    # Save page metadata\n    echo \"URL: $url\" \u003e \"$extract_dir/${sanitized_filename}_metadata.txt\"\n    echo \"Title: $title\" \u003e\u003e \"$extract_dir/${sanitized_filename}_metadata.txt\"\n    echo \"Extraction Date: $(date)\" \u003e\u003e \"$extract_dir/${sanitized_filename}_metadata.txt\"\n    \n    echo -e \"${GREEN}Successfully extracted content from $url${NC}\"\n    echo -e \"${GREEN}Saved to:${NC} $extract_dir/${sanitized_filename}_content.txt\"\n}\n\n# Process each URL\n",

      "codeBlock": {
        "contents": "\n\n/**\n * Deep research feature utilizing Firecrawl's latest API capabilities\n * This function can perform targeted extraction based on research categories\n * and provides different depth levels of analysis.\n */\nexport const deepResearch = async (\n\turls: string[],\n\toptions: DeepResearchOptions,\n) =\u003e {\n\tconst {\n\t\tdepth = ResearchDepth.MODERATE,\n\t\tcategories = [ResearchCategory.SIGHTINGS],\n\t\trecursiveLinks = false,\n\t\tlinkDepth = 1,\n\t\textractionModel = \"anthropic/claude-3-opus-20240229\",\n\t\tsearchParams = {},\n\t\tmaxResults = 10,\n\t} = options;\n\n\t// Adjust scraping parameters based on research depth\n\tconst depthConfig: Record\u003c\n\t\tResearchDepth,\n\t\t{ formats: Format[]; limit: number }\n\t\u003e = {\n\t\t[ResearchDepth.SURFACE]: {\n\t\t\tformats: [\"markdown\", \"extract\"],\n\t\t\tlimit: 50,\n\t\t},\n\t\t[ResearchDepth.MODERATE]: {\n\t\t\tformats: [\"markdown\", \"extract\", \"screenshot\"],\n\t\t\tlimit: 100,\n\t\t},\n\t\t[ResearchDepth.DEEP]: {\n\t\t\tformats: [\"markdown\", \"extract\", \"screenshot\", \"html\"],\n\t\t\tlimit: 250,\n\t\t},\n\t\t[ResearchDepth.COMPREHENSIVE]: {\n\t\t\tformats: [\"markdown\", \"extract\", \"screenshot\", \"html\", \"content\"],\n\t\t\tlimit: 500,\n\t\t},\n\t};",

        "contents": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nScraper script to extract data from UAP Database URLs and download all media\nusing the firecrawl library.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport json\nimport time\nimport requests\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional\nimport urllib.parse\n\ntry:\n    from firecrawl import FirecrawlApp\nexcept ImportError:\n    print(\"The 'firecrawl-py' package is not installed.\")\n    print(\"Please install it using: pip install firecrawl-py\")\n    exit(1)\n\n# Configuration\nAPI_KEY = os.environ.get(\"FIRECRAWL_API_KEY\")\nif not API_KEY:\n    print(\"ERROR: FIRECRAWL_API_KEY environment variable not set.\")\n    print(\"Please set your Firecrawl API key using:\")\n    print(\"export FIRECRAWL_API_KEY='your_api_key'\")\n    exit(1)\n\n# Output directories\nDATA_DIR = Path(\"data/uapdb_scrape\")\nMEDIA_DIR = DATA_DIR / \"media\"\nJSON_DIR = DATA_DIR / \"json\"\n\n# Create output directories if they don't exist\nos.makedirs(MEDIA_DIR, exist_ok=True)\nos.makedirs(JSON_DIR, exist_ok=True)\n\n# Initialize Firecrawl\napp = FirecrawlApp(api_key=API_KEY)\n\n# List of URLs to scrape\nwith open('uapdb_urls.txt', 'r') as f:\n    URLS = [line.strip() for line in f if line.strip()]\n\ndef sanitize_filename(url: str) -\u003e str:\n    \"\"\"Convert URL to a safe filename.\"\"\"\n    parsed = urllib.parse.urlparse(url)\n    path = parsed.path.rstrip('/').replace('/', '_')\n    query = parsed.query.replace('=', '_').replace('\u0026', '_') if parsed.query else \"\"\n    filename = f\"{path}_{query}\" if query else path\n    if not filename:\n        filename = \"index\"\n    # Extract the postid if available\n    if \"postid=\" in url:\n        postid = url.split(\"postid=\")[1].split(\"\u0026\")[0]\n        filename = f\"uapdb_post_{postid}\"\n    else:\n        filename = f\"uapdb_{filename}\"\n    return filename",

        "contents": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nScraper script to extract data from UAP Database URLs and download all media\nusing the firecrawl library.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport json\nimport time\nimport requests\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional\nimport urllib.parse\n\ntry:\n    from firecrawl import FirecrawlApp\nexcept ImportError:\n    print(\"The 'firecrawl-py' package is not installed.\")\n    print(\"Please install it using: pip install firecrawl-py\")\n    exit(1)\n\n# Configuration\nAPI_KEY = os.environ.get(\"FIRECRAWL_API_KEY\")\nif not API_KEY:\n    print(\"ERROR: FIRECRAWL_API_KEY environment variable not set.\")\n    print(\"Please set your Firecrawl API key using:\")\n    print(\"export FIRECRAWL_API_KEY='your_api_key'\")\n    exit(1)\n\n# Output directories\nDATA_DIR = Path(\"data/uapdb_scrape\")\nMEDIA_DIR = DATA_DIR / \"media\"\nJSON_DIR = DATA_DIR / \"json\"\n\n# Create output directories if they don't exist\nos.makedirs(MEDIA_DIR, exist_ok=True)\nos.makedirs(JSON_DIR, exist_ok=True)\n\n# Initialize Firecrawl\napp = FirecrawlApp(api_key=API_KEY)\n\n# List of URLs to scrape\nwith open('uapdb_urls.txt', 'r') as f:\n    URLS = [line.strip() for line in f if line.strip()]\n\ndef sanitize_filename(url: str) -\u003e str:\n    \"\"\"Convert URL to a safe filename.\"\"\"\n    parsed = urllib.parse.urlparse(url)\n    path = parsed.path.rstrip('/').replace('/', '_')\n    query = parsed.query.replace('=', '_').replace('\u0026', '_') if parsed.query else \"\"\n    filename = f\"{path}_{query}\" if query else path\n    if not filename:\n        filename = \"index\"\n    # Extract the postid if available\n    if \"postid=\" in url:\n        postid = url.split(\"postid=\")[1].split(\"\u0026\")[0]\n        filename = f\"uapdb_post_{postid}\"\n    else:\n        filename = f\"uapdb_{filename}\"\n    return filename",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "contents": "    echo \"$processed_urls\" | while read -r media_url; do\n        # Skip empty lines\n        [[ -z \"$media_url\" ]] \u0026\u0026 continue\n        \n        # Extract filename from URL\n        local filename=$(basename \"$media_url\" | sed 's/\\?.*//')\n        \n        echo -e \"${YELLOW}[$count/$url_count] Downloading:${NC} $filename\"\n        \n        # Download with curl, showing progress bar\n        curl -L --progress-bar \"$media_url\" -o \"$media_dir/$filename\"\n        \n        # Check if download was successful\n        if [[ $? -eq 0 ]]; then\n            echo -e \"${GREEN}Successfully downloaded:${NC} $filename\"\n        else\n            echo -e \"${RED}Failed to download:${NC} $filename\"\n        fi\n        \n        count=$((count+1))\n    done\n}\n\n# Function to use Firecrawl Extract API\nuse_firecrawl_extract() {\n    local url=\"$1\"\n    local domain=$(sanitize_domain_name \"$url\")\n    \n    echo -e \"${YELLOW}Using Firecrawl Extract API for $url...${NC}\"\n    \n    # Create domain-specific directory for multiple URLs\n    if [[ ${#URLS[@]} -gt 1 ]]; then\n        mkdir -p \"$DOWNLOAD_DIR/extracted/$domain\"\n        local extract_dir=\"$DOWNLOAD_DIR/extracted/$domain\"\n    else\n        local extract_dir=\"$DOWNLOAD_DIR/extracted\"\n    fi\n    \n    # Prepare the request to Firecrawl Extract API\n    local response=$(curl -s -X POST https://api.firecrawl.dev/v1/extract \\\n        -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n        -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" \\\n        -d \"{\\\"urls\\\": [\\\"$url\\\"], \\\"formats\\\": [\\\"all\\\"]}\")\n    \n    # Check if the API call was successful\n    if [[ $response == *\"error\"* ]];         ],
        "originalContents": "\n\n/**\n * Enhanced scrape function with optional FIRE-1 agent for advanced navigation.\n * @param url URL to scrape\n * @param options Scrape options\n * @param agent Optional FIRE-1 agent config ({ model: 'FIRE-1', prompt: string })\n * @returns Scraped content in requested formats\n * @example\n * await enhancedScrapeContent('https://example.com', { formats: ['html'] }, { model: 'FIRE-1', prompt: 'Click next until done.' })\n */\nexport const enhancedScrapeContent = async (\n\turl: string,\n\toptions: ScrapeOptions = {},\n\tagent?: { model: \"FIRE-1\"; prompt: string },\n) =\u003e {\n\tif (agent) options.agent = agent;\n\treturn await fireCrawl.scrapeUrl(url, options);\n};",

Remove duplicates\\n\\ndef extract_content(html_content):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Extract and structure content from the HTML.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    soup = BeautifulSoup(html_content, 'html.parser')\\n    \\n    # Extract title\\n    title_tag = soup.find('title')\\n    title = title_tag.text if title_tag else \\\"No title\\\"\\n    \\n    # Extract all text paragraphs\\n    paragraphs = []\\n    for p in soup.find_all('p'):\\n        paragraphs.append(p.get_text(strip=True))\\n    \\n    # Extract all headings\\n    headings = []\\n    for i in range(1, 7):  # h1 to h6\\n        for h in soup.find_all(f'h{i}'):\\n            headings.append({f'h{i}': h.get_text(strip=True)})\\n    \\n    # Extract all lists\\n    lists = []\\n    for ul in soup.find_all('ul'):\\n        items = [li.get_text(strip=True) for li in ul.find_all('li')]\\n        lists.append(items)\\n    \\n    # Extract all tables\\n    tables = []\\n    for table in soup.find_all('table'):\\n        table_data = []\\n        rows = table.find_all('tr')\\n        for row in rows:\\n            cols = row.find_all(['td', 'th'])\\n            cols_text = [col.get_text(strip=True) for col in cols]\\n            if cols_text:\\n                table_data.append(cols_text)\\n        if table_data:\\n            tables.append(table_data)\\n    \\n    # Structure the extracted data\\n    content = {\\n        \\\"title\\\": title,\\n        \\\"headings\\\": headings,\\n        \\\"paragraphs\\\": paragraphs,\\n        \\\"lists\\\": lists,\\n        \\\"tables\\\": tables\\n    }\\n    \\n    return content\\n\\ndef scrape_url(url, visited_urls, max_pages=100):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Scrape the given URL and recursively scrape any links found.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    if len(visited_urls) \u003e= max_pages:\\n        print(f\\\"Reached maximum pages limit ({max_pages})\\\")\\n        return\\n    \\n    if url in visited_urls:\\n        print(f\\\"Already visited: {url}\\\")\\n        return\\n    \\n    print(f\\\"Scraping: {url}\\\")\\n    visited_urls.add(url)\\n    \\n    try:\\n        # Extract and structure the content\\n        content = extract_content(html_content)\\n        \\n        # Save the structured content as JSON\\n        json_path = JSON_DIR / f\\\"{base_filename}.json\\\"\\n        with open(json_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:\\n            json.dump(content, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)\\n        \\n        # Find all links on the page\\n        links = extract_links(html_content, url)\\n        print(f\\\"Found {len(links)} links on {url}\\\")\\n        \\n        # Recursively scrape each link\\n        for link in links:\\n            if link.endswith(('.jpg', '.jpeg', '.png', '.gif', '.pdf')):\\n                continue  # Skip media files\\n            scrape_url(link, visited_urls, max_pages)\\n    \\n    except Exception as e:\\n        print(f\\\"Error scraping {url}: {e}\\\")\\n\\ndef main():\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Main function to scrape the UFO Evidence website.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    print(\\\"UFO Evidence Website Scraper\\\")\\n    print(\\\"===========================\\\")\\n    print(f\\\"Data will be saved to: {DATA_DIR}\\\")\\n    \\n    visited_urls = set()\\n    max_pages = 20\\n    \\n    start_time = time.time()\\n    scrape_url(MAIN_URL, visited_urls, max_pages)\\n    end_time = time.time()\\n    \\n    print(\\\"\\\\nScraping completed!\\\")\\n    print(f\\\"Pages scraped: {len(visited_urls)}\\\")\\n    print(f\\\"Time taken: {end_time - start_time:.2f} seconds\\\")\\n    print(f\\\"Results saved to: {DATA_DIR}\\\")\\n    \\n    # Save a summary report\\n    summary = {\\n        \\\"main_url\\\": MAIN_URL,\\n        \\\"pages_scraped\\\": len(visited_urls),\\n        \\\"scraped_urls\\\": list(visited_urls),\\n        \\\"timestamp\\\": time.time()\\n    }\\n    \\n    with open(DATA_DIR / \\\"scraping_summary.json\\\", 'w') as f:\\n        json.dump(summary, f, indent=2)\\n\\nif __name__ == \\\"__main__\\\":\\n    main()\"}",

There are rather well-authenticated cases spanning a wide variety of \\\"physical effects.\\\" Car-stopping cases are one important class. UFOs have repeatedly been associated with ignition failures and light-failures of cars and trucks which came near UFOs or near which the UFOs moved. I would estimate that one could assemble a list of four or five dozen such instances from various parts of the world. Interference with radios and TV receptions have been reported many times in connection with UFO sightings. There are instances where UFOs have been reported as landing, and after departure, holes in the ground, or depressions in sod or disturbed vegetation patterns have been described. In many such instances, the evident reliability of the witnesses is high, the likelihood of hoax or artifice small. A limited number of instances of residues left behind are on record, but these are not backed up by meaningful laboratory analyses, unfortunately.\\n\\nA physical effect that does not typically occur under conditions where the description of events might seem to call for it, relates to sonic booms. Although there are on record a few cases where fast-moving UFOs were accompanied by explosive sounds that might be associated with sonic booms, there are far more instances in which the reported velocity corresponded to supersonic speeds, yet no booms were reported. A small fraction of these can be rationalized by noting that the reporting witnesses were located back within the \\\"Mach cone\\\" of the departing UFO; but this will not suffice to explain away the difficulty. One feels that if UFOs are solid objects, capable of leaving depressions in soil or railroad ties when they land, and if they can dash out of sight in a few seconds (as has been repeatedly asserted by credible witnesses), they should produce sonic booms. This remains inexplicable; one can only lamely speculate that perhaps there are ways of eliminating sonic booms that we have not yet discovered; perhaps the answer involves some entirely different consideration.\\n\\nIf we include among \\\"physical effects\\\" those that border on the physiological, then there appear to be many odd types. Repeatedly, tingling and numbness have been described by witnesses who were close to UFOs; in many instances outright paralysis of a UFO witness has occurred. These effects might, of course, be purely psychological, engendered by fear; but in some instances the witnesses seem to have noted these effects as the first indication that anything unusual was occurring. A number of instances of skin-reddening, skin-warming, and a few instances of burns of very unusual nature are on record. These physiological effects are sufficiently diverse that caution is required in attempting generalization. Curiously, a peculiar tingling and paralysis seem to be reported more widely than any other physiological effects. A person who is almost unaware of the ramifications of the UFO evidence may think it absurd to assert that people have been paralyzed in proximity to UFOs; the skeptic might find it inconceivable that such cases would go unnoticed in press and medical literature. Far from it, I regret to have to say, on the basis of my own investigations. I have encountered cases where severe bodily damage was done, or where evident hazard of damage was involved, yet the witness and his family found ridicule mounting so much faster than sympathy that it was regarded wiser to quietly forget the whole thing. At an early stage of my investigations I would have regarded that as quite unbelievable; UFO investigators with longer experience than mine will smile at that statement, but probably they will smile with a degree of understanding. The most frequently claimed effects are electric or electromagnetic in nature. There are rather well-authenticated cases spanning a wide variety of \\\"physical effects.\\\"\\n\\n[![](http://www.ufoevidence.org/Researchers/ResearcherPics/Thumbs/JamesMcDonald.jpg)](http://www.ufoevidence.org/researchers/detail24.htm)\\n\\n#### James E. McDonald  ,   Ph.D.\\n\\n##### [author's bio](http://www.ufoevidence.org/researchers/detail24.htm)\\n\\n* * *\\n\\nAgain, the answer is that they do. There are rather well-authenticated cases spanning a wide variety of \\\"physical effects.\\\" Car-stopping cases are one important class. UFOs have repeatedly been associated with ignition failures and light-failures of cars and trucks which came near UFOs or near which the UFOs moved. I would estimate that one could assemble a list of four or five dozen such instances from various parts of the world. Interference with radios and TV receptions have been reported many times in connection with UFO sightings. There are instances where UFOs have been reported as landing, and after departure, holes in the ground, or depressions in sod or disturbed vegetation patterns have been described. In many such instances, the evident reliability of the witnesses is high, the likelihood of hoax or artifice small. A limited number of instances of residues left behind are on record, but these are not backed up by meaningful laboratory analyses, unfortunately.\\n\\nA physical effect that does not typically occur under conditions where the description of events might seem to call for it, relates to sonic booms. Although there are on record a few cases where fast-moving UFOs were accompanied by explosive sounds that might be associated with sonic booms, there are far more instances in which the reported velocity corresponded to supersonic speeds, yet no booms were reported. A small fraction of these can be rationalized by noting that the reporting witnesses were located back within the \\\"Mach cone\\\" of the departing UFO; but this will not suffice to explain away the difficulty. One feels that if UFOs are solid objects, capable of leaving depressions in soil or railroad ties when they land, and if they can dash out of sight in a few seconds (as has been repeatedly asserted by credible witnesses), they should produce sonic booms. This remains inexplicable; one can only lamely speculate that perhaps there are ways of eliminating sonic booms that we have not yet discovered; perhaps the answer involves some entirely different consideration.\\n\\nIf we include among \\\"physical effects\\\" those that border on the physiological, then there appear to be many odd types. Repeatedly, tingling and numbness have been described by witnesses who were close to UFOs; in many instances outright paralysis of a UFO witness has occurred. These effects might, of course, be purely psychological, engendered by fear; but in some instances the witnesses seem to have noted these effects as the first indication that anything unusual was occurring. A number of instances of skin-reddening, skin-warming, and a few instances of burns of very unusual nature are on record. These physiological effects are sufficiently diverse that caution is required in attempting generalization. Curiously, a peculiar tingling and paralysis seem to be reported more widely than any other physiological effects. A person who is almost unaware of the ramifications of the UFO evidence may think it absurd to assert that people have been paralyzed in proximity to UFOs; the skeptic might find it inconceivable that such cases would go unnoticed in press and medical literature. Far from it, I regret to have to say, on the basis of my own investigations. I have encountered cases where severe bodily damage was done, or where evident hazard of damage was involved, yet the witness and his family found ridicule mounting so much faster than sympathy that it was regarded wiser to quietly forget the whole thing. At an early stage of my investigations I would have regarded that as quite unbelievable; UFO investigators with longer experience than mine will smile at that statement, but probably they will smile with a degree of understanding. I could cite specific illustrations to make all this much clearer, but will omit them for space-limitations, except for a few remarks in the next section.\\n\",\"path\":\"packages/docs/UfoevidenceDoc616McDonald.md\"}",
